title: Range Addition II
summary: Given an m x n matrix M filled with zeros and an array of operations, each operation increments all elements in a submatrix defined by the operation.
statement: Given an m x n matrix M filled with zeros and an array of operations, each operation increments all elements in a submatrix defined by the operation. Count and return the number of times the maximum value appears in the matrix after applying all operations.
constraints: 1 <= m,n <= 40,000; each operation [a,b] satisfies 1 <= a <= m and 1 <= b <= n.
An operation increments the top-left a by b submatrix.
hints: Cells with the most increments must belong to every operated rectangle.
The common top-left rectangle has the smallest row and column limits.
If ops is empty return m*n; otherwise multiply the minimum a and minimum b.
All operation rectangles share exactly that minimum-size prefix, and no cell outside it receives every increment.
editorial: All operation rectangles share exactly that minimum-size prefix, and no cell outside it receives every increment.

tests.explanation: Only the overlapping 2 by 2 corner receives both increments, so it has the maximum count.
Without operations every cell remains at the same maximum value, so all nine cells count.
